analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md gets a date bump plus a new sentence around head line 170 saying a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, performLifecycleDrain). docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md gets a date bump and a wider description of when a drain can finish with coordinator_acknowledged=false: no registered session during startup, idle outside schedule, or reconnecting. The large head_text excerpts (lines 952-1550 of protocol-messages.md) are unchanged surrounding context; I read them against the threat model and found no changed security contract there. No code, wire fields, keys, attestation, authorization or cache behavior changes. No threat assumption is invalidated. Telemetry stays local and not uploaded, and the document says it carries no IDs, prompts or credentials. The drain text explicitly avoids claiming coordinator acknowledgement, which is consistent with TB-002 and with admission staying closed after a possible permanent fence. Remaining unverified contract: the real performLifecycleDrain behavior is not supplied. If an unregistered-session drain finished while local response writes or in-flight work were still active, that would be a code issue, but this PR gives no evidence of it. Threats checked: T-010 and T-053, for drain and cancellation lifecycle. No findings.
